% Ohm's law with resistivity
\begin{equation}\label{eq:C1_Ohm}
\mathbf{E} = -\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B} + \eta_O\,\mathbf{J},\ \mathbf{J} = \nabla\times\mathbf{B}
\end{equation}

% Induction with constant resistivity
\begin{equation}\label{eq:C1_induction_const}
\partial_t\mathbf{B} = \nabla\times(\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B}) + \eta_O\,\nabla^2\mathbf{B}
\end{equation}

% Induction with variable resistivity
\begin{equation}\label{eq:C1_induction_var}
\partial_t\mathbf{B} = \nabla\times(\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B}) + \eta_O\,\nabla^2\mathbf{B} - (\nabla\eta_O)\times\mathbf{J}
\end{equation}

% Joule heating
\begin{equation}\label{eq:C1_Q}
Q_{\mathrm{Ohm}} = \eta_O\,|\mathbf{J}|^2 \ge 0
\end{equation}

% Explicit CFL
\begin{equation}\label{eq:C1_CFL}
\Delta t \le (\Delta x)^2/(2\eta_O)\ \text{1D},\ (\Delta x)^2/(4\eta_O)\ \text{2D},\ (\Delta x)^2/(6\eta_O)\ \text{3D}
\end{equation}
